{{Short description|Archive of Rudolf Carnap in Pittsburgh}}
The '''Rudolf Carnap Papers''' are a large collection of documents and photographs that record much of the life and career of German philosopher [[Rudolf Carnap]]. They are used by scholars and historians not only for research into his life, but also for research into his theories and the theories of other scholars with whom he corresponded. The Carnap papers are restored, maintained, cataloged and housed in the [[Archives Service Center, University Library System, University of Pittsburgh]]. They include extensive correspondence, lecture outlines for courses that he taught, and drafts of his published works and unpublished manuscripts. Much of the content of the Rudolf Carnap papers is available electronically and searchable through the archive.<ref> {{cite web
| url = http://www.calstatela.edu/sites/default/files/dept/phil/pdf/res/Carnap-Elimination-of-Metaphysics.pdf|title=The Elimination of Metaphysics Through Logical Analysis of Language|postscript=; translated from the German, Erken11t11i.r, Vol. II (1932) by Arthur Pap| access-date = 2015-12-02 }}</ref> His work on metaphysics being essentially a question of semantics is still cited and have been further expanded by other scholars.<ref>{{cite web | title =Philosophy Review&nbsp;— Philosophical Methodology; The Armchair or the Laboratory?|last=Haug|first=Matthew C.|date=10 March 2015|volume=19|number=11|postscript=; Review by Jamie Carlin Wastson|url = http://metapsychology.mentalhelp.net/poc/view_doc.php?type=book&id=7352
| access-date = 2015-12-02 }}</ref> 

His papers document why he is considered a major contributor to the study of [[metaphysics]]. He was also a member of the [[Vienna Circle]].<ref>{{cite web | title = A Little History of Philosophy by Nigel Warburton&nbsp;– review | url = https://www.theguardian.com/books/2011/sep/01/little-history-philosophy-warburton-review |work=The Guardian|date=1 September 2011|access-date=2 December 2015 | first = Julian | last = Baggini }}</ref>

==History of the collection==
The papers were donated by Carnap's daughter Hanna Carnap-Thost in 1974.<ref>
{{cite web | title = Rudolf Carnap Papers, 1905-1970, ASP.1974.01, Special Collections Department, University of Pittsburgh|publisher=Guides to Archives and Manuscript Collections at the University of Pittsburgh Library System |
url=http://digital.library.pitt.edu/cgi-bin/f/findaid/findaid-idx?c=ascead;type=simple;q1=Philosophy%20of%20Science;rgn=Entire%20Finding%20Aid;size=25;view=reslist;subview=standard;cc=ascead;sort=occur;start=1;didno=US-PPiU-asp197401;focusrgn=admininfo;byte=46386577#| access-date = 2015-12-02 }}</ref>

==Scope of the collection==
The collection is used by those researching personal information and the subjects covered by the collection.<ref>{{cite book | last = Parrini | first = Paolo | title = Logical empiricism : historical & contemporary perspectives | publisher = University of Pittsburgh Press | location = Pittsburgh | year = 2003 | isbn = 9780822941941 }}</ref><ref name="AwodeyCarus2006">{{cite journal|last1=Awodey|first1=S.|last2=Carus|first2=A. W.|title=Carnap's dream: Gödel, Wittgenstein, and Logical, Syntax|journal=Synthese|volume=159|issue=1|year=2006|pages=23–45|issn=0039-7857|doi=10.1007/s11229-006-9066-4|doi-access=free}}</ref> The scope of the collection is quite large and contains information on the following subjects
